trial_court: Second Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Durg, in civil suit No.119-A/2014
case_name: Vivek Singh vs Yogendra Singh Thakur
facts_of_case: Appellant and late wife were married on 23-6-2007. Late wife committed suicide on 3-1-2009. Respondent claimed return of properties gifted to his daughter at the time of marriage. Appellant objected to jurisdiction of Family Court.

legal_principles.principle: The Family Court can only assume jurisdiction if there is a dispute between the parties to a marriage with respect to their marital status, divorce, restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, child custody, maintenance, or property sharing.
legal_principles.held: But, in no event, the Family Court can have jurisdiction if the above dispute is absent. By no stretch of imagination, can the Family Court assume jurisdiction, if there is a dispute between the brothers, sisters, mothers, fathers etc. concerning property and the case on hand being one such, the Family Court had clearly no jurisdiction.

legal_principles.principle: The Family Court's jurisdiction is limited to suits and proceedings between the parties to a marriage with respect to their property or of either of them.
legal_principles.held: A plain reading of the provisions would manifest that for maintaining a suit or proceeding of the nature mentioned in Explanation (c) sub-section (1) of Section 7 of the Act, 1984, the suit or proceeding has to be between the parties to a marriage with respect to the property of the parties or of either of them.

outcome.result: Appeal preferred by husband challenging judgment and decree of trial court allowing suit for return of properties
outcome.final_order: Court allowed appeal, set aside judgment and decree of trial court, and remanded matter back to trial court for fresh decision.
